t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop website section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on a warm limestone ground. Small wordmark and section label over a hairline rule, then a two-line light-weight sans headline. Left two thirds: a hairline table with slash-numbered rows and monospace cells for <CONTENT>. Right: a square-cornered muted steel-blue readout tile with one oversized light numeral and a mono unit, a fine tick scale along its foot with a single limit line and a small outlined limit tag. Faint off-white pipe elbow line art behind the tile, bleeding off the edge. Flat, no shadows.
signature_idea: A trace table ends in one instrument readout: the requirement's number shown as a meter with its limit tick, so the claim looks measured.
strengths: readout tile is a strong, reusable key-figure device
table is genuinely structured: rows by document, columns by requirement
brand type system is right: light headline, mono figures, sentence case
ghost pipework adds context without clutter
one accent block on limestone keeps it calm
weaknesses: readout figure equals the limit, so the scale tells no story
tile and tag corners are slightly rounded
table is dense mono text and close to plain table
ghost pipes are decorative and connect to nothing
brand_fit_why: Limestone, navy text, one steel-blue tile, light headline and mono figures match the brand book; only slight rounding and table density detract.
